name: Anduril Industries
product: Lattice software fuses sensor data and coordinates autonomous air, land and maritime systems built by Anduril and partners.
targetCustomer: US and allied defense and national-security agencies
buyer: Defense ministries, military services and program offices
fundingDisplay: $5B Series H; cumulative funding not disclosed in the cited announcement
traction: The US Army awarded Team Anduril a signed $99.6M, 11-month OTA prototype agreement for NGC2 in July 2025; this is a prototype agreement, not an IDIQ ceiling.
notes: Full-stack software, sensors and vehicles support a 5/5 integration score. The company reports $2.2B 2025 revenue, but that figure is company-reported and is not inferred from contract ceilings. US military exports can require ITAR/EAR licensing; classified deployments and procurement accreditation constrain GTM.

name: Shield AI
product: Hivemind is an autonomy stack for aircraft and other robotic systems; Shield AI also builds the V-BAT vertical-takeoff UAS.
targetCustomer: US and allied military operators and defense-platform manufacturers
buyer: Defense ministries, military services and aerospace OEMs
fundingDisplay: $240M Series F-1; cumulative funding not disclosed in the cited announcement
traction: The US Navy selected Shield AI for a multi-vendor ISR services IDIQ with an aggregate ceiling of up to $800M; Shield AI must compete for task orders, and no Shield-specific obligation is disclosed in the cited notice.
notes: Autonomy software that transfers across platforms plus owned aircraft creates a strong but not fully captive stack. The $800M Navy figure is a vendor-pool ceiling, not an award or backlog attributable to Shield AI. ITAR/EAR, airworthiness, spectrum and weapons-release rules can restrict deployment and exports.

name: Saronic Technologies
product: Saronic builds autonomous surface vessels and Echelon command-and-control software for distributed maritime operations.
targetCustomer: US and allied navies and maritime-security agencies
buyer: Naval acquisition commands and defense ministries
fundingDisplay: $1.75B Series D; cumulative funding not disclosed in the cited announcement
traction: The US Navy selected Saronic among seven vendors for at-sea MUSV testing in 2026; the Navy states that only vendors successfully completing the test receive the $15M award and production eligibility.
notes: Vessel design, manufacturing, autonomy and fleet C2 support a 5/5 integration score. Navy marketplace selection is conditional and is not yet a $15M order; no company-specific task order is inferred. Maritime weapons, autonomy, spectrum and ITAR/EAR rules remain material export and deployment constraints.

sources.label: US Navy MUSV marketplace test selection

name: Vannevar Labs
product: Vannevar builds software that combines public, commercial and operational data for maritime awareness, targeting support and other national-security missions.
targetCustomer: US and allied defense and national-security organizations
buyer: Operational commands, intelligence organizations and defense program offices
fundingDisplay: $75M Series B; cumulative funding not disclosed in the cited announcement
traction: Vannevar reports that its agentic-AI capabilities were deployed and tested during Talisman Sabre 2025; exercise participation is a technical signal, not evidence of a disclosed procurement order.
notes: The moat depends on classified-workflow integration and accumulated mission data more than owned hardware. Public sources do not disclose a current contract value or headcount. Data rights, security accreditation, classification and ITAR/EAR constrain customer access and international expansion.

name: CHAOS Industries
product: Vanquish is a coherent distributed radar architecture intended to detect and track drones, missiles and aircraft with networked low-cost nodes.
targetCustomer: US and allied air-defense and critical-infrastructure operators
buyer: Defense ministries, military services and security agencies
fundingDisplay: >$1B total funding
traction: CHAOS and Forterra report field testing an integrated autonomous counter-UAS system; this is a partnership and test signal, not a disclosed government purchase.
notes: FundingUsdM is a conservative lower bound because the company says it has raised more than $1B. A referenced $10M congressional appropriation for radar development is not treated as a CHAOS contract or revenue. Radar spectrum rules, security accreditation and ITAR/EAR can constrain deployments and exports.

name: Epirus
product: Leonidas is a software-defined high-power microwave system designed to disable groups of electronic threats such as drone swarms.
targetCustomer: US and allied air-defense forces and critical-infrastructure operators
buyer: Military acquisition offices and defense ministries
fundingDisplay: >$550M total venture funding
traction: The US Army signed a $43,551,060 base contract in July 2025 for two IFPC-HPM Generation II systems, testing, support and spares; additional systems are options rather than committed base orders.
notes: FundingUsdM is a lower bound because the announcement states more than $550M. Purpose-built semiconductors, emitters, software and system integration justify the 5/5 scores. Directed-energy safety, spectrum, military export licensing and ITAR/EAR are material constraints.

name: Forterra
product: AutoDrive is a platform-agnostic autonomy stack for military and commercial ground vehicles, including operation in GPS-denied environments.
targetCustomer: Defense vehicle OEMs, military operators and industrial fleets
buyer: Military program offices, defense primes and fleet operators
fundingDisplay: $75M Series B; cumulative funding not disclosed in the cited announcement
traction: In August 2025 the US Army awarded three autonomy OTAs to Forterra, Overland AI and Scout AI with approximately $15.5M aggregate value; Forterra's individual amount is not public.
notes: Platform breadth and OEM integration support strong scores, while dependence on partner vehicles limits full vertical control. Company-reported system and mission counts are not translated into revenue. Autonomous-vehicle safety, military qualification, cyber accreditation and ITAR/EAR constrain adoption and export.

sources.label: US Army aggregate autonomy OTA announcement

name: Overland AI
product: OverDrive provides autonomy for off-road vehicles and OverWatch provides mission command for heterogeneous robotic ground fleets.
targetCustomer: US and allied land forces and defense-vehicle manufacturers
buyer: Army program offices, defense ministries and vehicle OEMs
fundingDisplay: $32M Series A; cumulative funding not disclosed in the cited announcement
traction: Overland received an $18.6M-ceiling Army prototype OT in 2024; the ceiling is potential value, not disclosed obligated spend. A later Army notice reports $15.5M aggregate across three vendor OTAs without allocating Overland's share.
notes: The headcount is the company's approximate figure at the Series A date. Strong research-led off-road autonomy is balanced by early manufacturing scale and reliance on vehicle partners. OTA ceilings must not be treated as revenue; ITAR/EAR, safety qualification and government cyber controls apply.

sources.label: US Army aggregate autonomy OTA announcement

name: Second Front Systems
product: Game Warden is a managed DevSecOps and deployment platform for bringing commercial software into accredited government cloud, on-premise and edge environments.
targetCustomer: Software vendors and US and allied government organizations
buyer: Government CIOs, program offices and commercial software vendors
fundingDisplay: $70M Series C; cumulative funding not disclosed in the cited announcement
traction: USAspending identifies a $2,819,975 Game Warden delivery order for 2024-2026; this is an actual order under the contract vehicle, not the vehicle's overall ceiling.
notes: The moat is accreditation and distribution into restricted environments rather than proprietary AI research, hence 2/5 vertical integration. Customer counts on the company blog are self-reported. FedRAMP/DoD authorization, classified-network access, data residency and export-control obligations are core GTM constraints.

name: True Anomaly
subsector: Autonomous orbital vehicles and space-domain awareness
product: True Anomaly combines Jackal autonomous orbital vehicles with Mosaic mission software for space-domain awareness and proximity operations.
targetCustomer: US and allied space-security organizations
buyer: Space-force acquisition commands, intelligence agencies and satellite operators
fundingDisplay: >$1B total capital; Series D includes $50M debt
traction: True Anomaly signed a $30M Space Systems Command contract for VICTUS HAZE and committed a further $30M of private capital to the $60M effort.
notes: FundingUsdM is a lower bound and includes disclosed debt. The $1.8B Andromeda program referenced by the company is a program/IDIQ ceiling and is not attributed to True Anomaly absent task-order data. Space licensing, rendezvous-and-proximity safety, debris liability, spectrum and ITAR/EAR constrain operations and exports.

name: Array Labs
subsector: Formation-flying radar satellites and 3D Earth intelligence
product: Array Labs is developing clusters of formation-flying radar satellites to produce high-resolution 3D imagery and moving-target intelligence.
targetCustomer: Defense, intelligence, mapping and infrastructure organizations
buyer: Government geospatial-intelligence programs and commercial data customers
fundingDisplay: $35M total funding
traction: A federal SBIR record supports funded development of Array's 3D SAR processing; public sources do not establish scaled recurring revenue or a large production order.
notes: Funding total is explicitly stated by the company. Formation flying plus proprietary radar processing is technically deep but pre-scale, so execution and launch risk remain high. Remote-sensing licensing, spectrum allocation, orbital-debris rules and export controls can restrict data products and hardware sales.

fundingDisplay: €600M Series D; cumulative funding not disclosed in the cited announcement
